title: Building Reliable Classes
lede: Turn Week 5's class syntax into working models: define valid state, preserve it through methods, trace references, separate shared data from instance data, and connect objects through composition.

sections.title: Contracts and valid state
concepts: Start with a promise

A class is useful when it gives the rest of the program a dependable promise. A stock item starts with a non-negative quantity; a successful withdrawal reduces it by exactly the requested positive amount; a rejected withdrawal changes nothing. These rules are its invariant and method contract.

Write down the inputs, result and state change before writing the method body. Test zero, negative amounts, exactly the available quantity and one too many. A getter reports a value; a mutator changes the model. Keeping these jobs clear makes a failing test easier to explain.
Hide the path around the rule

Java private prevents an outside caller from assigning a field directly. Python _stock communicates intended use but does not enforce privacy. In either language, public methods should be the normal route for changing state. Constructor validation must establish the same invariant that later methods preserve; these small examples assume a valid starting quantity.

concepts: Draw objects separately from names

b = a copies a reference in both languages. Draw two arrows to one object, then trace a mutating call through either arrow. Creating another object requires another constructor call. Two objects with equal field values need not be the same object.
Instance collections belong in the constructor

sections.title: Shared data and instance data
concepts: A counter is a deliberate shared responsibility

A shared ticket counter is appropriate when every new ticket must receive the next number. The ticket's own number is instance data. Updating the shared counter later does not rewrite existing ticket numbers.
Mutation differs from rebinding

Appending to a shared class list changes that one list. Assigning a.items = [] instead creates an instance attribute that shadows the class attribute for a. This is why the location of allocation matters more than whether the expression contains an object name.

sections.title: Composition and a small public interface
concepts: A has-a relationship

A shelf holds a book; it is not a special kind of book. A field that refers to another object expresses this composition. Give the class with the data the job that uses it: Book knows its title, while Shelf decides how to describe its contents.
Make observations easy

A useful string representation helps a person inspect state while debugging. Return a string from __str__; do not print inside it. In Java the corresponding method is toString(). Keep presentation separate from the operations that update the model, so a formatting change does not change the rules.

questions.correct: Zero, because the contract requires a positive amount.

questions.correct: It prevents outside code from directly assigning the field.
wrong: It automatically rejects every negative value passed to any method of the class.

It makes all stock objects share one common copy of the private field.

questions.correct: A shelf has a book.

exercises.solution:
class Inventory:
    def __init__(self, stock): self._stock = stock
    def take(self, amount):
        if amount <= 0 or amount > self._stock: return False
        self._stock -= amount
        return True
    def available(self): return self._stock

item = Inventory(int(input()))
n = int(input())
for _ in range(n):
    print("OK" if item.take(int(input())) else "Refused")
print(item.available())

title: Lists and Generics
lede: Replace fixed-size arrays with collections, compare ArrayList and LinkedList, distinguish positions from values, and use type parameters to reuse code without giving up type checking.

sections.title: ArrayList and Python lists
concepts: A sequence that grows

An array has a fixed length. An ArrayList manages a backing array and its capacity for you, so adding an element does not require you to allocate a replacement yourself. size() is the number of stored elements; capacity is internal storage, not a set of elements you can already access.
Insert, replace and inspect

Use add(value) to append, add(index,value) to insert and set(index,value) to replace. Valid access indices run from 0 through size−1. Insertion also permits size, which appends. Python uses append, insert and bracket assignment for the corresponding jobs.

sections.title: Removal and safe traversal
concepts: Overloading can change meaning

On ArrayList<Integer>, remove(1) removes index 1; remove(Integer.valueOf(1)) removes the first value equal to 1. The argument type decides the overload. A value removal that finds no match returns false; a position outside the list is an error.
Do not shift the ground under your loop

Removing from a list while an enhanced for-loop is traversing it can invalidate the traversal. Use an Iterator and its remove method, iterate indices backwards, or create a filtered result. The Python example creates a new list, so repeated adjacent rejected values are handled correctly.

sections.title: Linked nodes and queues
concepts: Follow links instead of shifting values

A linked list stores nodes with links between them. Java LinkedList is doubly linked. Adding or removing at an end does not shift a backing array, but reaching the node at an arbitrary index still requires traversal. A fast unlink after finding a node does not make every remove(index) constant time.
Choose from the access pattern

ArrayList is a sound default for indexed access and ordinary traversal. LinkedList offers operations at both ends. Repeated get(i) in a loop can make a linked-list traversal quadratic; an enhanced for-loop visits it sequentially. For a Python FIFO queue, collections.deque avoids repeatedly shifting the front of a list.

sections.title: Type parameters and programming to List
concepts: Reuse behaviour while retaining types

Box<T> describes one class parameterised by a reference type. Box<String> accepts strings and returns a String. A raw Box would discard useful checking. Primitive types cannot be type arguments: use Integer rather than int. Boxing and unboxing bridge the two, but unboxing a null Integer fails.
Separate the operation from storage

A method accepting List<Integer> can work with ArrayList or LinkedList when it needs only the List operations. Neither List<Integer> nor List<Double> is a subtype of List<Number>. Generic type arguments are invariant. This page introduces the idea; wildcard bounds and type erasure are further reading.

title: Inheritance, Interfaces and Polymorphism
lede: Describe a shared contract, implement it in several classes, and trace which method runs. Compare Java inheritance and interfaces with Python inheritance, abstract base classes and duck typing.

sections.title: Inheritance and construction
concepts: An is-a relationship

Inheritance describes a specialised kind of an existing type. A Dog is an Animal. Java uses extends and allows one direct superclass; Python lists base classes in parentheses. Constructors establish a valid base part as well as any added subclass state. Java constructors are not inherited.
Use the parent without duplicating it

super(name) invokes a superclass constructor in Java. Python super() provides the next implementation in the method resolution order. Overriding lets a subclass specialise an inherited instance method while retaining the shared operation that callers expect.

sections.title: Dispatch and abstract classes
concepts: Declared type versus object type

The declared type of a Java variable determines which members a call may refer to. For an overridden instance method, the actual object selects the implementation at runtime. Field access and static methods do not follow that same dynamic-dispatch rule. Overloading is also chosen using compile-time argument types.
Incomplete does not mean useless

An abstract class can hold state, a constructor and concrete methods while requiring subclasses to implement certain operations. It cannot be instantiated directly. Python's abc module provides ABC and abstractmethod for an enforced version of that contract. A class with only an informal method that raises NotImplementedError does not enforce the same instantiation restriction.

sections.title: Interfaces and behavioural contracts
concepts: Specify an operation without choosing storage

A Java interface specifies a type that classes may implement independently of their single superclass. Implementations of its abstract public methods must be public. Interfaces have no per-object instance fields, but can have constants and default methods; they are more than an informal list of names.
A common caller needs only the promise

A shape-area loop does not need to know each concrete shape. In Python, the caller can simply require an area or send method, without a common base class. This is duck typing: the required operations matter. It remains the programmer's responsibility to keep the behaviour and argument expectations consistent.

sections.title: Composition, final and multiple inheritance
concepts: Use inheritance for substitutable types

A Notice uses a delivery channel; it is not a kind of channel. Composition keeps the delivery choice replaceable. Java final on a class prevents subclassing; final on an instance method prevents overriding. A final reference still permits mutation of the object it refers to.
Trace the actual lookup order

Python permits multiple inheritance, so super means the next implementation in the MRO, not always one fixed parent. Inspect __mro__ for the order. For introductory designs, a small interface or a composed helper often communicates the intended collaboration more clearly than a complicated hierarchy.

lede: Handle expected failures deliberately, follow exceptions through method calls, and read tokens or lines without losing data. Connect in-memory readers to real file input in Java and Python.

sections.title: Expected failures and specific handlers
concepts: A failure changes control flow

An exception is an object reporting a failed operation. When it is thrown or raised, the current path stops and control searches for a matching handler. Statements after the failing operation in the try block are skipped. A syntax error is different: the program must first be valid code before normal exception handling can run.
Catch what you can explain

Catch NumberFormatException around integer conversion in Java, or ValueError in Python. A broad catch that silently ignores everything can hide bugs outside the expected failure. Python's else suite separates successful parsing from work that should not be covered by the conversion handler.

sections.title: Propagation, checked exceptions and cleanup
concepts: Throw here, handle at the right level

A Java checked exception must be caught or declared with throws. RuntimeException and its subclasses are unchecked. The declaration tells a caller what may propagate; it does not catch the exception. Cleanup is separate from success

For closeable resources, prefer Java try-with-resources and Python with instead of hand-writing a fragile sequence of closes.

sections.title: Tokens, lines and end of input
concepts: Choose a reading contract

A Scanner token read skips delimiters. A line reader preserves the distinction between an empty line and no line. Decide whether your input is a token stream, line records or free text before choosing an API. The line boundary may carry meaning that tokenisation discards.
Do not confuse a blank line with EOF

BufferedReader.readLine returns null at end of input. Python file iteration simply ends. Python readline returns an empty string at EOF but returns a newline character for a blank line. Use the exact EOF contract of the chosen API. The Python method is spelled readline(), not readLine.

title: Writing Files and Reliable Reports
lede: Choose a text format, write complete records, close resources, and check what a later reader receives. Separate computation from presentation so reports can be tested without depending on a real file.

sections.title: Output is a data contract
concepts: Write the format down first

A report intended for another program needs a defined field order, delimiter, encoding and newline policy. Human-readable object display is not automatically a stable storage format. Keep the calculation separate from formatting and keep formatting separate from the destination.
print, println and write

Java PrintWriter offers print and println. Python write emits exactly the string supplied; it does not insert a separator or newline. An in-memory StringWriter or StringIO makes the stored output visible without depending on an external file. The same distinction matters when writing to a file.

sections.title: File modes, closing and error reporting
concepts: Overwrite and append are different promises

Opening Python text in w mode truncates an existing file; a mode appends. Java new PrintWriter("report.txt") also truncates an existing file. For appending in Java, wrap a suitable append-mode writer, such as new FileWriter("report.txt", true). Choose the mode deliberately before opening a file.
Close before checking the saved result

Buffered output can remain unwritten until flushing or closing. try-with-resources and with arrange cleanup when leaving scope. PrintWriter is unusual: many write methods record errors rather than throwing IOException, so checkError is needed when the program must detect a failed write. Closing a resource does not prove the data was valid or the whole operation succeeded.

sections.title: Responsibility and information experts
concepts: A coherent reason to change

A class should model one coherent responsibility. This does not mean one method per class. A model may need constructors, queries and updates that all preserve the same rules. Receipt wording, storage format and price calculations can change for different reasons; separating them limits the consequences of each change.
Put a calculation beside its information

GRASP's Information Expert suggests assigning behaviour to the object that has the needed information. A line knows price and quantity, so it computes a subtotal. An order knows its lines, so it sums their subtotals. It need not reach inside every line's fields or repeat the subtotal rule.

A basket that depends on a PriceRule can accept another rule without editing its calculation. This is a concrete way to keep a stable caller while extending a policy. The abstraction earns its place when there are real alternatives; creating an interface for every class is not the goal.

Dependency inversion asks high-level policy to depend on the needed abstraction, not a specific low-level implementation. Passing the collaborator through a constructor makes that choice explicit. Python can use a callable for a small policy. A function may be a clearer design than a hierarchy when there is one operation.

Liskov substitution concerns behaviour: a replacement must preserve expectations that make callers correct. A List implementation whose add unexpectedly prepends would violate callers relying on append order. Java's type checker can check method signatures, but it cannot prove every business rule.
Expose only the capability a caller uses

Interface segregation keeps clients from depending on unrelated operations. A notifier needs send, not an entire storage, configuration and user-management service. concepts: Coordinate without owning every rule

A controller can translate a request into model operations and a response. Keep the inventory rule in Stock; the controller should not duplicate its availability calculation. High cohesion groups related work; low coupling keeps each component dependent on as few details as it needs.
Keep one source of each rule

DRY avoids duplicating a piece of knowledge in several places. Similar-looking code is not always the same rule, so extract a helper when the meaning is shared. YAGNI cautions against implementing speculative features. GRASP also names Creator, Polymorphism, Pure Fabrication, Indirection and Protected Variation; use those roles to explain a design, not to force extra layers into a small program.

concepts: Use the state you can observe

For a loop, name what the accumulator means after each iteration. A pass counter counts passing values in the processed prefix, not the remaining suffix. State the index range and boundary condition before predicting the output. Exactly 50 is a useful test because it distinguishes ≥ from >.
Separate mutation from rebinding

Method and function calls pass values; when a value is an object reference, both caller and parameter can identify the same object. Mutating that object is visible through both names. Reassigning the local parameter chooses another value for that local name. Explain these as two different operations rather than saying that a language passes every object by reference.

sections.title: Test boundaries and explain causes
concepts: A test should distinguish a mistake

Useful cases include no data, one item, the exact boundary, one below it, duplicates, a blank line, and a final record without a newline. For a mutator, inspect the resulting state as well as the return value. A test that passes even when the intended rule is removed is weak evidence.
Explain from input to consequence

A code explanation should name the relevant state, condition or dispatch decision, then connect it to the next visible result. Avoid merely restating each line. For a bug, give a small counterexample, identify the first incorrect state transition, propose the correction and predict its effect on the counterexample.

sections.title: Optional: functional ideas and streams
concepts: A new way to express a familiar traversal

Ed's Beyond Programming 1 lessons introduce first-class functions, pure transformations and stream pipelines. A filter selects elements; a map transforms them; a reduction combines results. A stream pipeline has intermediate operations and a terminal operation. These ideas express computations already possible with loops.
Preview, not a new assessment specification

The Java example uses Java 8 stream operations and Arrays.asList so it remains compatible with this website. It avoids later APIs such as List.of and Stream.toList. The Python function constructs a fresh result without modifying its input. This section is optional enrichment; current Canvas instructions determine assessed scope.

questions.q: Which test directly distinguishes >=50 from >50?
questions.correct: A mark equal to 50.
wrong: A mark equal to 85, since both comparisons disagree for every passing mark.
An empty list, since its missing mark is automatically treated as exactly fifty.
A mark equal to zero, since both comparisons disagree for every failing mark.
questions.why: Only the equality boundary distinguishes these two comparisons.

questions.q: What count should a summary of valid records use?
questions.correct: The number of records that passed parsing and validation.
wrong: The number originally declared by the input, even when some of those records were rejected.
The number of diagnostic messages, because each diagnostic represents one valid record.
The number of fields on the last line, because it determines the size of the whole dataset.
questions.why: Attempted input count and successful record count can differ.

questions.q: What makes a code explanation useful?
questions.correct: It connects a concrete state or rule to the observed result.
wrong: It repeats every punctuation mark aloud while avoiding the values used by the program.
It states that the code works because the output looked plausible on one ordinary input.
It describes only formatting choices and never mentions control flow or changing state.
questions.why: A causal explanation shows why a result follows and helps predict changed inputs.

questions.q: What do the optional stream examples change about the computation?
questions.correct: They express selection and aggregation with a pipeline.
wrong: They remove the need for any decisions or repeated processing of data elements.
They guarantee that invalid input can never produce an exception in any program.
They make the original source list shrink whenever an element fails the filter.
questions.why: Streams express familiar traversal operations. The example does not mutate its source list.
